messages:
alyssa: Quick question for the group — thinking about the operator <> autoscaler surface for Dedicated GPU pools. We keep hitting edge cases where the operator owns lifecycle (node pools, taints, image updates) but the autoscaler needs richer signals (tenant headroom, prewarm credit, tenant SLA). How tightly should we couple the APIs? :thinking:
omar: my instinct is to keep a small, explicit contract: operator exposes PoolStatus + AdmissionHint and the autoscaler writes PoolIntent. Operator reconciles actual machines. That way rollouts stay operator-local and autoscaler can request capacity without mutating low-level infra.
jeff: can you sketch the fields? short list is fine.
alyssa: sketch — PoolIntent { desired_capacity, burst_credit_request, priority_class } and PoolStatus { allocatable_gpus, drained_gpus, prewarm_count, last_update }
sara: +1. also need a clear fallback for when operator denies intent (e.g., quota/region limits). autoscaler should be able to read denial_reason and fall back to model-variant routing.
kg: important tradeoff: if autoscaler can force-provision (operator executes) we get faster response but risk cross-tenant cost spikes. If autoscaler can only request and operator vetoes, we get safer ops but more latency. We should support both modes behind a config flag (force_provision=true for enterprise tenants).
alyssa: agreed. propose defaults: tenant_force=false, but expose policy at PoolIntent.level. also require audit log for any force_provision.
nora: how do we account prewarm credits? current billing model assumes reserved capacity. If autoscaler prewarms ephemeral nodes we need amortization. Maybe autoscaler attaches a PrewarmTicket with duration and expected tokens.
omar: something like: 
```
PoolIntent {
  desired_replicas: 8,
  prewarm_tickets: [ {id: "t-123", slots:2, expires_at: 1700000000} ],
  priority: "realtime"
}
```
jeff: sounds fine. I want to flag complexity: reconciliation loops can conflict if operator's internal drain is async. Need leasing—operator should expose a Lease object per node (or per slab) so autoscaler can make atomic handoffs.
sara: yes, Lease TTL + renew semantics. If autoscaler can't renew (operator drains) we should surface a metric and backoff.
kg: is this a new CRD? PoolIntent/PoolStatus/PoolLease? I'm worried about proliferation. Could we piggyback on existing ScaleIntent CRD and add fields?
alyssa: we can extend existing ScaleIntent but keep a namespaced PoolIntent for operator-only semantics. Smaller incremental API is easier. Also add versioning header so we can opt in to new semantics.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: applied PoolIntent rev=v2 for pool=dedicated-east-3 at 2304506798
omar: edge case — partial admission: operator may grant fewer GPUs than requested. autoscaler must have a deterministic backoff and split remaining request across other pools or fallback to lower-qos model. Must avoid thrashing.
jeff: suggest exponential backoff with jitter + credit accounting: if partial_grant < request, reduce request by allowed_fraction and requeue remainder after backoff. Also mark tenant as prewarmed=false if prewarm tickets not honored.
nora: + add a metric: pool.partial_grants.count and a per-tenant prewarm_rejections metric. needed for SRE alerts.
sara: ops safety: any force_provision path must require a signed approval token for changes that exceed daily cost threshold. Not for normal autoscale ops, only for manual/force.
alyssa: next steps: 1) I'll draft a short proto API (PoolIntent/PoolStatus/PoolLease) and a compatibility plan to extend ScaleIntent, 2) Omar and Jeff can sketch operator lease semantics, 3) KG + Nora to propose metering fields for billing and alerts. We'll sync Thursday 10am.
kg: ok. one more ask — add a simple JSON example of denial_reason so product can wire fallback messages to customers.
alyssa: example: `{"denial_reason":"quota_exceeded","details":"region-east has 0 GPUs left for tenant"}`
omar: perfect. I'll add this to the proto doc.
jeff: minor: include a replay-safe event_id on PoolIntent so we can reconcile idempotently when controllers crash.
sara: can someone file a short RFC link? I can shepherd.
alyssa: filing now — will post link in thread when done. :thumbsup:
